body.statement: The certificate criterion is necessary and sufficient: \(\mathsf C(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1\) if and only if \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\). On the affirmative side, \(\mathsf A\) returns \(\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}\); on the negative side, it returns \(\mathsf{Wit}_{T,S,B}\). This equivalence holds simultaneously for every endpoint coordinate \(Q_a(x)\) and every positive law, including null allowed-arrow effects and deficient observable-kernel ranks.
body.justification: An iff theorem distinguishes a design rule from another sufficient recovery recipe and makes failure operational through a legal countermodel.
body.gap: Theorems 1--6 of Tikka and Karvanen neither use partial audit margins nor characterize intervention-target identification; Levis et al. require full phase-two recovery.
body.consumer: The theorem decides whether a planned partial recontact protocol supports the five-year treatment-specific weight distribution in an EHR cohort under the declared local dropout graph.
